title: KV cache consistency and degraded-read backoff guide
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview: This guide defines the detection, containment, and remediation patterns we use when the LLM KV (key-value) cache exhibits consistency or availability problems that cause degraded reads (stale or missing KV state). It explains automated degraded-read backoff behavior, operator remediation steps, configuration knobs, and dashboards/alerts to ensure predictable failover without violating tenant SLOs. Scope: - Applies to the distributed LLM KV prefix cache used by the serving runtime (global name: runtime-kv-cache). - Covers transient network partitions, metadata index corruption, leader election flaps, and partial shard availability. - Excludes full model binary corruption and hardware-level memory errors (see eng-serving-runtime/known-issues). Owner and responders: - Primary owner: eng-platform (runtime-ops squad) - Oncall rotation: platform-operator (pager) -> eng-sre escalation -> runtime-infra engineering - Notification channels: #platform-ops, #oncall-pager, paged phone roster Definitions and failure modes: 1) Missing-KV reads: requests that expect a cached KV entry but receive a cache-miss where a valid entry should exist. 2) Stale-KV reads: reads that return older prefix state due to replication lag or divergent leadership. 3) Partial-shard-unavailable: a subset of shards return 5xx or time out. 4) Consistency-mismatch: divergence between metadata index and stored shard contents resulting in incorrect routing or invalid tokenization offsets. Detection signals (metrics & logs): - metric/runtime_kv_read_error_rate (per-shard, p95) - metric/runtime_kv_stale_read_ratio (synthetic checks comparing authoritative source to cache) - metric/runtime_kv_replication_lag_seconds (95/99) - logs: "KV_MISMATCH", "KV_SHARD_OOS", leader-change events in audit logs - synthetic canaries: canary-prefix-check- (compare authoritative prefix store -> cache) Alerting rules and dashboard guidance: - Alert: KV-SHARD-ERROR-CRITICAL - Trigger: shard error rate > 0.5% for 5m AND p95 latency > 250ms - Severity: P1 (page) - Alert: KV-READ-DEGRADED-WARN - Trigger: aggregated stale_read_ratio > 0.2% for 10m OR replication_lag_seconds p99 > 3s - Severity: P2 (slack) - Dashboard panels to include: - per-shard read error heatmap - multi-region canary diff (ratio of mismatches) - recent leader-change timeline annotated with deploys - operator mitigation knobs (current backoff multiplier, degraded-serving-mode) Containment and automated degraded-read backoff pattern (high level): 1) Detect anomalous shard behavior using the synthetic canary and metric gates. 2) Automatically place affected shard(s) into "degraded-read-backoff" mode rather than immediate eviction when: - read_error_rate spike OR replication_lag > configurable threshold AND - model SLO indicates a better UX serving slightly stale responses vs 5xx errors. 3) In degraded-read-backoff mode, the runtime will: - apply exponential read delay/queuing for new requests targeting that shard (config: backoff_base_ms, max_backoff_ms) - fall back to last-known-good (LKG) prefix state if the request decoder accepts slightly older KV state (config: allow_stale_prefix=true for non-strict routes) - stream partial outputs with a header: X-Redwood-KV-State: degraded/LKG
This behavior reduces 5xx storms, prevents cascading load onto healthy shards, and buys time for automated healing. Config table (recommended defaults): | knob | description | default | |------|-------------|---------| | backoff_base_ms | base backoff delay applied on first degraded read | "20" | | max_backoff_ms | maximum per-attempt backoff to avoid request starvation | "2000" | | backoff_multiplier | exponential multiplier per retry | "2.0" | | allow_stale_prefix | whether to serve last-known-good prefix on degraded read | "true" | | degraded_mode_min_duration_s | minimum time to stay in degraded mode before re-eval | "30" | | degraded_mode_probe_interval_s | frequency of probes to check shard recovery | "10" | | stale_tolerance_seconds | maximum age of LKG prefix allowed | "5" | (Operator note: the runtime accepts these via the /api/v1/ops/kv-config endpoint. Example YAML below.) YAML example (ops config push): ```yaml kv_backoff: backoff_base_ms: 20 max_backoff_ms: 2000 multiplier: 2.0 allow_stale_prefix: true min_duration_s: 30 probe_interval_s: 10 stale_tolerance_seconds: 5 ``` Automated remediation actions (order of operations): 1) Probe: controller runs an immediate consistency probe against the shard (reads canonical store and compares prefixes). 2) Soft-redirect: route a percentage of traffic to compatible model-variant replicas in the same region (variant-candidates list maintained by model-onboarding). See routing policy example below. 3) If probes pass -> transition out of degraded mode. 4) If probes fail for > 3 probes spaced by probe_interval -> start controlled re-synchronization job for shard (resync ownership -> rehydrate cache from authoritative store). 5) If re-sync fails or OOS count > threshold -> schedule shard replacement/rehoming (operator intervention required). Routing policy example (OPA / policy hint): - Prefer: same-region compatible-variant -> preferred-latency < 50ms - Fallback: cross-region cold-variant (only when allow_cross_region_fallback=true and tenant policy allows) Operator runbook (step-by-step): 1) Triage 1. Acknowledge page. Post immediate summary in #platform-ops with shard and region, include alert runbook link. 2. Check dashboard panels: per-shard heatmap, leader-change log, probe history. 2) Immediate containment (automated but verify): 1. Confirm degraded-read-backoff mode enabled for affected shard via API: curl -sS https://ops.internal/v1/kv/shards//status 2. If not enabled, enable with: curl -X POST https://ops.internal/v1/kv/shards//degraded -d '{"mode":"backoff"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 3) Investigate root cause: - Review shard logs for KV_MISMATCH and leader-election flaps. - Run a targeted probe: /tools/kv_probe --shard --compare-authoritative true --output json 4) Repair path options (pick one): A) Quick rehydrate: trigger cache rehydrate job for shard (if probe shows missing entries). Command: /ops/bin/rehydrate_shard --shard --type incremental B) Rehome: if leader flapping, reassign leader and wait for stable leader epoch. Command: /ops/bin/rehome_shard --shard --target-node C) Full resync: schedule full resync job during low-traffic window and notify SRE. Use: /ops/bin/full_resync --shard --window_start --dedupe true 5) Monitor recovery: probe-to-success ratio should reach 1.0 for three consecutive probes spaced by probe_interval_s before clearing alerts. 6) Post-incident checklist: create retrospective (template below), tag runbook with lessons and any configuration changes. Escalation matrix and SLAs: - If P1 persists > 15 minutes without improved probe results -> page runtime-infra lead and eng-sre manager. - If degraded mode remains > 2 hours -> schedule customer-impact investigation with customer-success for tenants impacted by strict-consistency routes. Testing and validation (pre-deploy & chaos): - Unit tests: simulate kv-backoff with synthetic requests asserting that no more than 1% of requests see 5xx under injected 10% shard error. - Chaos tests: orchestrate shard flaps via canary chaos runner: cause leader-flap, confirm degraded-mode triggers and traffic falls back to LKG without customer-visible 500s. - Load tests: verify degraded backoff increases tail latency by < 20% for affected routes and reduces 5xx rate by > 95%. Dashboard and alert implementation details (Grafana/Prometheus): - Query examples: - Read error rate per shard: sum(rate(runtime_kv_read_errors_total[5m])) by (shard) / sum(rate(runtime_kv_reads_total[5m])) by (shard) - Stale read ratio (canary diff): sum(canary_mismatch_total) / sum(canary_probe_total) - Alert escalation note: alerts should include a direct link to the probe job and the current degraded-mode flags to reduce cognitive load. Release, rollout, and operator training: - Feature flag: kv-degraded-backoff-v2. Roll out in three phases: internal canary -> regional canary -> global. - Training: 45-minute ops workshop for platform-operators covering: runbook walk-through, probe tools, and rehome commands. Record session and attach to team-wiki. Retrospective template (to complete after incidents): 1) Incident summary (one-paragraph) 2) Timeline of key events (alerts, mode changes, operator actions) 3) Root cause analysis (technical) 4) Detection gaps and suggested metric additions 5) Configuration changes made and rationale 6) Action items, owners, due dates 7) Follow-up verification steps and cost/latency impact post-remediation Appendix: example incident timeline snippet - 2027-02-03 03:14 UTC: KV-READ-DEGRADED-WARN alert fired for shard-12 (us-west) - 03:16 UTC: controller enabled degraded-read-backoff for shard-12 automatically - 03:17 UTC: probe failed (missing prefixes), rehydrate job scheduled - 03:28 UTC: rehydrate completed, probe green at 03:30 UTC -> degraded mode cleared Contacts and links: - Runtime-ops runbook index: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks - Oncall rota: /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/operator-oncall-quick-reference-shell-helpers-and-scripts-2026 - Tooling: /internal/tools/kv_probe (README attached on team drive) Change history: - 2027-01-14: created by Maya Patel (draft) - 2027-02-01: rewrote containment strategy to prefer LKG + backoff (reviewers Diego Martinez, Hannah Lee) - 2027-02-09: published after chaos-tests and led a training session
